newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to attend Hong Kong ceremony - Howard.
newsitem.headline: Australia to attend Hong Kong ceremony - Howard.

text.p: Australia will attend the swearing in of Hong Kong's new Beijing-appointed legislature next month, rejecting the U.S. and British boycott for the sake of its own national interest, Prime Minister Howard said on Thursday.
"I don't disguise the fact that China is a very illiberal, undemocratic country," Howard said in a television interview. "Of course it is."
"But my responsibility is to look to the national interest and it is in Australia's national interest to build a sound relationship with China."
The appointed legislature, replacing the elected chamber that Britain established in Hong Kong, will be sworn in on July 1 after China resumes control of the 156-year-old British colony.
The United States said on Tuesday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would attend the handover ceremony but not the swearing in of the legislature.
Britain followed on Wednesday by saying Prime Minister Tony Blair would also miss the legislature ceremony.
But Howard, justifying his decision, said on Thursday that Australia needed a close economic relationship with China.
Maintaining good relations with China was also more useful in campaigning to improve Beijing's approach to human rights, he added.
Western countries including Australia have criticised Beijing's decision to replace the current legislature with a new provisional legislature of 400 members.
The Australian Labor Party opposition has demanded that Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer, representing Australia at the handover, also boycott the ceremony.
Earlier on Thursday China shrugged off the U.S. and British snubs.
China had invited 4,000 people to attend the ceremony and the absence of a few individuals would not prevent it going off smoothly, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman said at a briefing.
